summaryText:
Pastor Travis taught from Isaiah 6 and Isaiah 10:27, John 11, and Luke 5 on the question, "What would happen if God really showed up?" He challenged the church to move beyond attending a service as a routine and to long for a real encounter with God. He explained the anointing as the manifested presence and power of the Holy Spirit in and over a life, and he taught that it destroys yokes of bondage rather than simply managing them. He named burdens such as anxiety, shame, guilt, pride, insecurity, and addiction, and said that when God shows up, chains do not just weaken but break.

He offered three things that happen when God shows up. First, God reveals what has been hidden. Using Isaiah's vision of the Lord on the throne, Pastor Travis noted that the closer Isaiah came to God's holiness, the more aware he became of his own sin. God encountered him, exposed him, and cleansed him, then called him with the words, "Whom shall I send?" Pastor Travis stressed that God exposes us to heal us, not to shame us, and that healing begins with honesty. He also reminded listeners that God already knows what we try to hide and still loves us. He invited anyone who felt led to take the step of water baptism, as it was baptism Sunday.

Second, God rearranges your life. An encounter with God is never neutral and always calls for a response. Pastor Travis pointed to Moses, Joshua, Elijah, and the disciples, and spent time on Peter in Luke 5. After a miraculous catch, Peter left his boats and followed Jesus, because he had found someone greater than the miracle. The blessing is no longer the point, the Blesser is.

Third, God gets the final say. In the story of Lazarus in John 11, Jesus waited two days because he loved them, and by the time he arrived the situation looked hopeless. Pastor Travis encouraged those who feel that God is too late for a marriage, a family member, a diagnosis, or a long struggle that what looks dead to us is an opportunity for God to reveal his glory. He closed with a prayer of hope: it is not over, God is not done yet, and God knows exactly the right time. The service also announced the upcoming August series, My Wounds Won't Win.
mainPoints: When God shows up, he reveals what is hidden: he exposes our hearts not to shame us but to heal, cleanse, and prepare us for his purpose.
When God shows up, he rearranges your life: an encounter with God always calls for a response, and the Blesser matters more than the blessing.
When God shows up, he gets the final say: what looks dead or too late to us is an opportunity for God to reveal his glory and bring new life.

versesMentioned.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing.

In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord, high and exalted, seated on a throne; and the train of his robe filled the temple. Above him were seraphim, each with six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying. And they were calling to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty; the whole earth is full of his glory." At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook and the temple was filled with smoke.
"Woe to me!" I cried. "I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Almighty."

Then one of the seraphim flew to me with a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with tongs from the altar. With it he touched my mouth and said, "See, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away and your sin atoned for."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?" And I said, "Here am I. Send me!"
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

Jesus replied: "'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.' This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'"
"Do not come any closer," God said. "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground."

But if serving the Lord seems undesirable to you, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your ancestors served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you are living. But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.
Elijah went before the people and said, "How long will you waver between two opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal is God, follow him." But the people said nothing.
"Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people."
As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax collector's booth. "Follow me," he told him, and Matthew got up and followed him.
At this the man's face fell. He went away sad, because he had great wealth.

As he neared Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" "Who are you, Lord?" Saul asked. "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting," he replied.

When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch." Simon answered, "Master, we've worked hard all night and haven't caught anything. But because you say so, I will let down the nets." When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break. So they signaled their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
Then Jesus said to Simon, "Don't be afraid; from now on you will fish for people."
So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him.
So the sisters sent word to Jesus, "Lord, the one you love is sick."
Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. So when he heard that Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was two more days,
"Lord," Martha said to Jesus, "if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
"Take away the stone," he said. "But, Lord," said Martha, the sister of the dead man, "by this time there is a bad odor, for he has been there four days."
Then Jesus said, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"

When he had said this, Jesus called in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!" The dead man came out, his hands and feet wrapped with strips of linen, and a cloth around his face. Jesus said to them, "Take off the grave clothes and let him go."

Monday.scripture: Isaiah 6:3 (NIV): "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty; the whole earth is full of his glory."
Monday.focus: Seek God's presence, not just a routine. Welcome God to show up in your week.
Monday.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today with no phone. Ask God to show up in your heart, home, and relationships, and name one burden you want to hand over to him.
Monday.prayer: Lord, you are holy. I want more than a routine. Please show up in my life this week. I place my burdens before you and ask you to move in me. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Isaiah 6:5 (NIV): "Woe to me!" I cried. "I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips... and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Almighty."
Tuesday.focus: Honesty before God. Healing begins when we stop hiding.
Tuesday.action: Write down one thing you have been avoiding bringing to God. Tell him about it plainly, and if it helps, share it with a trusted believer or pastor for prayer.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I stop hiding and look at my own heart. Show me what needs your healing, and give me the courage to be honest. Thank you that you love me and do not leave me as I am. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Isaiah 6:7 (NIV): "See, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away and your sin atoned for."
Wednesday.action: After confessing to God today, speak this verse out loud over yourself. Then let go of one thing you have been carrying as guilt or shame.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, thank you that my guilt is taken away and my sin is atoned for. Cleanse my heart and my words today, and help me walk in freedom. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Luke 5:11 (NIV): "So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him."
Thursday.focus: Say yes to God. The Blesser matters more than the blessing.
Thursday.action: Ask God what he may be asking you to surrender or rearrange, such as a habit, a schedule, or a priority. Take one small, concrete step of obedience today.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, you are greater than any blessing. Show me what to loosen my grip on, and give me a willing heart to follow you. My answer is yes. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 11:40 (NIV): "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
Friday.focus: Hope when something looks dead or too late. God gets the final say.
Friday.action: Choose one situation that feels hopeless and pray over it for a few minutes. Write down, "It is not over, God is not done yet," and place it where you will see it.
Friday.prayer: Lord, you are never late. I bring you what looks dead and trust you with it, in your timing. Reveal your glory, and strengthen my faith while I wait. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Isaiah 6:8 (NIV): "Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?' And I said, 'Here am I. Send me!'"
Saturday.focus: Answer God's call with a yes and prepare to be sent.
Saturday.action: Encourage or serve one neighbor, friend, or family member today. Then invite someone to join you for worship this weekend or to watch next week's service online.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, here am I, send me. Use my life to love my neighbor and point others to you. Prepare my heart to worship you and to follow where you lead. Amen.
